title: The rise of the $100-billion RWA perp market
gist: Onchain perpetual futures tied to traditional assets (RWA perps) grew 44x in a year to $117.3B monthly volume, with onchain venues (now 86% of the market) overtaking centralized exchanges after Hyperliquid's HIP-3 upgrade, while the traded mix shifted from commodities toward equities.

insights.claim: Monthly trading volume in real-world-asset (RWA) perpetual futures reached $117.3 billion in August 2026, up 44x from a year earlier.
insights.speaker: a16z crypto editorial
insights.so_what: A 44x volume increase in one year signals RWA perps are moving from niche to a real venue for traditional-asset exposure onchain, worth tracking as a growth vector for crypto infrastructure and exchange revenue.
insights.quote: monthly RWA perp trading volume reached $117.3 billion in August, up 44x in a year

insights.claim: RWA perp monthly volume peaked at $145.1 billion in July 2026 before pulling back to $117.3 billion in August.
insights.speaker: a16z crypto editorial
insights.so_what: A pullback from a July peak suggests volume growth, while structurally rising, is not monotonic and could see episodic contractions worth monitoring rather than assuming a straight-line trend.
insights.quote: It continued climbing to $145.1 billion in July before pulling back to $117.3 billion in August.
insights.locator: After a down month in April

insights.claim: Open interest in RWA perps grew almost 30x, from $161 million in July 2025 to $4.8 billion in August 2026, and stayed near that record even as trading volume fell in August.
insights.speaker: a16z crypto editorial
insights.so_what: Open interest holding near highs while volume dips implies traders are keeping positions on rather than closing out, a sign of sticky rather than purely speculative flow-through demand.
insights.quote: RWA perp "open interest" ... climbed from $161 million in July 2025 to $4.8 billion in August 2026, increasing nearly 30x.

insights.claim: RWA perp volume remains small relative to traditional derivatives, where futures and options trade in the tens of trillions of dollars per month.
insights.speaker: a16z crypto editorial
insights.so_what: The current scale gap versus tens-of-trillions traditional derivatives markets frames RWA perps as still early-stage, implying large runway if the format keeps gaining share of traditional-asset trading.
insights.quote: RWA perp trading volume remains small compared with traditional derivatives markets, where futures and options trade in the tens of trillions of dollars per month
insights.locator: RWA perp trading volume remains small

insights.claim: Onchain venues now account for 86% of RWA perp trading volume, versus roughly two-thirds or more handled by centralized exchanges as recently as November 2025.
insights.speaker: a16z crypto editorial
insights.so_what: A flip from centralized-exchange dominance to 86% onchain share in under a year is a structural share shift worth pricing into which infrastructure captures fee/volume growth going forward.
insights.quote: By August, these venues were processing 86% of RWA perp volume, or roughly $101 billion, compared with about $16 billion on centralized exchanges.
insights.locator: Early on, RWA perp trading mostly happened

insights.claim: Centralized-exchange RWA perp volume peaked in March 2026 and declined through July while onchain volume kept climbing.
insights.speaker: a16z crypto editorial
insights.so_what: A declining centralized-exchange trend alongside rising onchain volume is a divergence signal that the marginal RWA perp trader is choosing onchain venues by preference, not just by availability.
insights.quote: Centralized exchange volume peaked in March and declined through July, while onchain volume continued to climb.

insights.claim: Only one venue is currently approved to offer a true perpetual futures contract to U.S. persons; most centralized and all decentralized exchanges restrict U.S. access to these products.
insights.speaker: a16z crypto editorial
insights.so_what: Regulatory restriction of U.S. persons from most RWA perp venues means the growth documented here is largely a non-U.S. phenomenon, a gap that could close if U.S. approvals expand.
insights.quote: only one venue has been approved to trade one perp at this time. All other centralized and decentralized exchanges restrict U.S. persons’ access to true perpetual futures contracts.

themes.theme: Hyperliquid's HIP-3 as the onchain catalyst

insights.claim: The shift toward onchain RWA perp trading aligns with Hyperliquid's October 2025 launch of HIP-3, which lets builders deploy their own perpetual futures markets on the network's shared HyperCore infrastructure.
insights.speaker: a16z crypto editorial
insights.so_what: If HIP-3 is the structural unlock for onchain RWA perps, Hyperliquid's shared infrastructure becomes a chokepoint worth watching for fee capture and for competitors replicating the builder-deployed-market model.
insights.quote: Hyperliquid’s October 2025 launch of HIP-3, an upgrade that lets builders deploy their own perpetual futures markets using the network’s shared trading infrastructure (HyperCore)
insights.locator: The timing of this shift aligns

insights.claim: RWA perp volume across onchain venues quadrupled to about $4 billion in October 2025 shortly after HIP-3 launched, and by December onchain venues handled about half of tracked RWA perp trading.
insights.speaker: a16z crypto editorial
insights.so_what: The rapid onchain volume ramp immediately following HIP-3 supports treating that upgrade as the specific trigger rather than a coincidental trend, useful for anticipating effects of similar infrastructure launches elsewhere.
insights.quote: RWA perp volume quadrupled to about $4 billion in October. By December, onchain venues handled about half of tracked RWA perp trading.
insights.locator: RWA markets, among the first builder deployments

themes.theme: Asset mix shift from commodities to equities

insights.claim: The RWA perp asset mix shifted from 84% commodities a year ago to 48% equities, 28% commodities, and 18% indices by August 2026.
insights.speaker: a16z crypto editorial
insights.so_what: Traders migrating from commodity to equity RWA perps suggests onchain demand is increasingly about replicating stock-market exposure, a signal for which traditional asset classes onchain infrastructure should prioritize next.
insights.quote: As of August this year, equities make up 48% of volume, compared with 28% for commodities and 18% for indices.
insights.locator: What people are trading has also changed

insights.claim: Equity open interest surpassed commodity open interest in June 2026 ($1.6B vs $1.2B), a month before equity trading volume overtook commodities.
insights.speaker: a16z crypto editorial
insights.so_what: Open interest leading volume in the equities-over-commodities shift suggests positioning data can be a leading indicator of where RWA perp trading flow is about to concentrate.
insights.quote: Equity open interest passed commodities in June, at $1.6 billion vs. $1.2 billion. A month later, equity trading volume passed commodities.
insights.locator: This shift toward equities showed up

themes.theme: Round-the-clock trading and structural differences from traditional futures

insights.claim: RWA perps have no scheduled expiration and some venues offer 24/7 trading, including weekends when traditional commodity futures and stock exchanges are closed.
insights.speaker: a16z crypto editorial
insights.so_what: Weekend and after-hours access to traditional-asset exposure is a structural feature traditional exchanges don't offer, a persistent edge for onchain venues even if regulatory or liquidity gaps narrow elsewhere.
insights.quote: Unlike conventional futures, they don’t have a scheduled expiration, and some venues also offer 24-hour trading, seven days a week.

insights.claim: The open question raised by RWA perp growth is whether these instruments become a standard offering at traditional brokers and exchanges.
insights.speaker: a16z crypto editorial
insights.so_what: If traditional brokers adopt RWA-perp-like products, incumbent exchanges could face competitive pressure on hours and margin structure from crypto-native venues that proved the demand first.
insights.quote: The next question is whether RWA perps become a standard offering at traditional brokers and exchanges.
